subject: Re: Migration/compat evaluation - OpenAI-compatible tests & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Natalie O'Connor <natalie@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration/compat evaluation - OpenAI-compatible tests & next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Natalie — good conversation and great signal on the migration priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations: 

Summary from call:
- FinCo priority: minimize changes to app code, keep prompt behavior close to current outputs, and lock down security/compliance for enterprise data flows.
- Key ask: compatibility with your current OpenAI-based integration (API surface / SDK swap) and a clear migration matrix showing where prompts behave differently.

How Redwood is thinking about the evaluation (recommended triage):
1) OpenAI-compatible smoke tests (low friction) — run the same curl/SDK calls against Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a handful of representative prompts and compare outputs, latency, and token usage.
2) SDK swap in staging — a minimal code change (client import + endpoint) to validate retry/streaming behavior and errors under real traffic. We can provide a staging key and a one-line SDK diff.
3) Prompt-diff and edge-case tests — run your existing prompt set, and we’ll flag tokenization/detokenization diffs and any hallucination/regression patterns.

Concrete next steps I propose (and owners):
- FinCo: share 8–12 representative prompts (sensitive items redacted) and a point of contact for procurement/security (Natalie).
- Redwood (Marissa): provide the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, sample curl/SDK snippet, and attach a migration matrix template.
- Redwood (Rishi): provision a staging key + canary route and run the SDK swap test (ETA 3 business days).

Initial tests we’ll run (examples):
- Smoke curl (OpenAI-compatible):
  curl https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <STAGING_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","prompt":"${PROMPT}","max_tokens":256}'

- SDK swap example (Node):
  // original: openai.ChatCompletion.create(...)
  // new: redwood.chat.completions.create(...)
  // we'll provide a 1-file diff and test harness.

Attachment: migration-matrix.csv (template) and redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf (one-pager on differences: latency/cost controls, batching/caching, rollout patterns).

Questions / open items:
- Do you have a strict API compatibility requirement (exact token parity) or tolerance for small prompt diffs if behavior is equivalent?
- Procurement: who should I loop in for an initial MSA/PO conversation?

Proposed schedule:
- FinCo shares prompts by EOD Friday (May 15)
- Redwood completes smoke/start-up tests and shares findings by Tue May 18 (we can also present in a short follow-up demo)

I'll attach the files to this thread and follow up with the staging key in a separate (secret) email.

Thanks — speak soon.

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise GTM | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0132

Attachment stubs: migration-matrix.csv (CSV), redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf (PDF)

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. Confirming the plan from our side. A couple of clarifications: 

- We can share 10 sample prompts by EOD Friday; they include a mix of customer-facing Q&A, billing/usage summary prompts, and internal admin prompts. We will redact customer identifiers.
- Procurement: loop in our legal/procurement lead (jcrawford@finco.com) for MSA/PO coordination. We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an IL4-ish data handling description.
- Timeline: can we target the smoke test next Monday (May 18) morning ET? That works better for our engineers.

Sample prompts (quick preview):
1) "Summarize the customer's invoices for April 2026 and highlight any late payments."
2) "Write a polite outreach to a customer with an overdue billing item."
3) "Given the following transaction logs (redacted), flag potential fraud indicators."

Also: one question on parity — are there any known differences in tokenization or default stop sequences we should be aware of? If so, please call them out in the migration matrix.

I'll share the prompts and loop in JC Crawford on the procurement thread. Looking forward to the Monday test.

Thanks,
Natalie
VP Product Operations | FinCo
Natalie.OConnor@finco.com
